pharm: Bacteriostatic (bactericidal at high concentrations) against gram-positive cocci; inhibits bacterial protein synthesis
quick: IM 600 mg q12-24h; IV 600 mg-1 g q8-12h
Parenteral; oral forms taken on empty stomach
Crosses placenta; use only if clearly needed
Reduce dose in severe impairment; monitor
summary: Lincomycin is a lincosamide antibiotic for serious infections caused by susceptible streptococci, pneumococci, and staphylococci, reserved for penicillin-allergic patients or where a penicillin is inappropriate. It carries a boxed warning for Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhea/colitis, which can be severe and fatal. Discontinue if significant diarrhea occurs and avoid use for minor or viral infections. Dose by infection severity and route, with reductions in severe renal or hepatic impairment.
indications: Serious infections due to susceptible streptococci, pneumococci, and staphylococci
Reserved for penicillin-allergic patients or where a penicillin is inappropriate
Adjunct to indicated surgical procedures for serious gram-positive infection

dosage.n: More severe: every 12 hours or more often
Up to 8 g/day IV in life-threatening situations
More severe: every 12 hours or more often

dosage.d: Dilute; infuse each 1 g over at least 1 hour
dosage.n: Never give as undiluted IV bolus (cardiopulmonary risk)

admin: Never administer intravenously as an undiluted bolus - dilute and infuse slowly (>=1 h per gram)
Discontinue immediately if significant diarrhea develops
Reserve for serious infections where less toxic agents are inappropriate
Reduce dose in severe renal or hepatic impairment
moa: Binds the 50S ribosomal subunit of susceptible bacteria, inhibiting peptidyl transferase and bacterial protein synthesis; primarily bacteriostatic but bactericidal at higher concentrations against susceptible gram-positive organisms.

absolute: Minor bacterial infections or viral infections (not indicated)
relative: History of gastrointestinal disease, especially colitis
Neonates (benzyl alcohol preservative - gasping syndrome risk)
monitor: Diarrhea / signs of C. difficile colitis
CBC with periodic counts in prolonged therapy

preg: No adequate well-controlled studies; crosses the placenta (cord serum ~25% of maternal). Contains benzyl alcohol preservative. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed.
lact: Reported in human milk (0.5-2.4 mcg/mL). Because of potential serious reactions in the infant, decide whether to discontinue nursing or the drug, weighing importance to the mother.
renal: Reduce dosage in severe renal impairment; serum half-life is prolonged. Use approximately 25-30% of the normal dose in severe renal impairment.
hepatic: Reduce dosage in severe hepatic impairment; monitor LFTs as hepatic accumulation may occur.

major: Neuromuscular blocking agents - lincomycin has neuromuscular blocking properties that may enhance their effect
moderate: Antiperistaltic antidiarrheals (e.g., loperamide) - may prolong/worsen C. difficile colitis
minor: Other antibacterials - generally compatible; avoid bacteriostatic-bactericidal antagonism where relevant
interactions.food: Oral absorption reduced by food; parenteral forms unaffected
interactions.diagnostics: May elevate LFTs; can cause leukopenia/neutropenia/thrombocytopenia on monitoring labs

serious: Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhea / pseudomembranous colitis (can be fatal)
Severe cutaneous reactions (SJS/TEN, AGEP, exfoliative dermatitis)
Blood dyscrasias (neutropenia, agranulocytosis, aplastic anemia, thrombocytopenic purpura, pancytopenia)
Cardiopulmonary arrest with rapid IV undiluted administration

monitoring: Diarrhea and signs of C. difficile colitis (even weeks after therapy)
counsel: Report diarrhea promptly, especially if severe, bloody, or with cramping - even after finishing therapy
Do not take anti-diarrheal medicines without advice
Report rash, itching, difficulty breathing, or swelling immediately
This drug is reserved for serious infections when penicillins are not suitable
Inform clinicians of any prior reaction to clindamycin
pk: IM ~11.6 mcg/mL at 60 min; IV (2 h infusion) ~15.9 mcg/mL
Therapeutic levels ~14-20 h after IM dose
pearls: Lincosamide - shares cross-resistance and C. difficile risk with clindamycin
Never give undiluted IV bolus: risk of severe cardiopulmonary reactions/arrest
Reserve for penicillin-allergic patients or where penicillin is inappropriate (stewardship)
Discontinue at once if significant diarrhea occurs - do not use antiperistaltic agents
missed: For a missed scheduled dose, administer as soon as possible; if near the next dose, skip and resume the regular schedule. Do not double doses. Parenteral dosing is managed by the care team.
overdose: Hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis are not effective in removing lincomycin. Management is supportive; monitor for and manage colitis, blood dyscrasias, and hypersensitivity.
